deli.title:
Délicorner — a B2B portal,
a design system, and an AI copilot
deli.subtitle: Freelance Product Designer mission at Délicorner (B2B foodtech, ~30 people). Two flagship deliverables in parallel: Corner Digital, the client portal and its design system built from scratch, and CX Copilot, a Slack AI bot that unclogs support and fights churn.
deli.role.value: Freelance Product Designer — DS, UX, AI
deli.mission.title: Two tracks, one standard
deli.mission.p1: Délicorner delivers premium food products in B2B and was running a client-portal MVP with a freelance PM, with no design foundation. I took on two fronts: structuring the product and its design system to make it testable and production-ready, then tackling an operational pain point — CX team overload — with an AI copilot.
deli.mission.p2: Both cases deliberately follow the same arc — Problem → Approach → System → Result — because they answer the same conviction: good design removes friction, whether in the interface or in the process.
deli.case1.title: B2B client portal & design system, from zero to shipped in 2 weeks
deli.case1.sub: A design-to-code pipeline built for speed without sacrificing rigour.
deli.c1.problem.title: The problem
deli.c1.problem.p1: Délicorner had to launch Corner Digital with no design system: a corporate brand guide existed, but no systematised product foundation. The design layer was missing — the one that lets you both test fast with real users and ship developers something reusable, consistent and production-ready.
deli.c1.problem.challenge.label: The challenge:
deli.c1.problem.challenge.text: turning a static brand guide into a living, accessible system that tech can leverage with AI — on a very tight deadline.
deli.c1.approach.title: The approach
deli.c1.approach.intro: Six steps, from token to an AI-ready design system:
deli.c1.s1.d: A DTCG-standard token file derived from the brand guide. A single, scalable source of truth.
deli.c1.s2.d: Pulls components from Storybook into Figma, wired to the same tokens, in 1 click. A free alternative to story.to.design.
deli.c1.s3.d: A genuinely functional high-fidelity proto for testing, built from the PM's MVP.
deli.c1.s4.d: Sessions with 3 clients (Hellowork, NVIDIA, Databricks) to surface friction before industrialisation.
deli.c1.s5.d: Variables, tokens, styles, components — with Claude Code, aligned to the tech stack: Angular, Tailwind, DaisyUI (naming included).
deli.c1.s6.d: DS structured for assisted generation (Figma Make, Claude Code, Codex): the design → dev → AI loop is closed.
deli.c1.system.title: The system
deli.c1.system.p1: The core: a single token propagates to N components, synced in one click across Storybook, code and Figma.

deli.case2.title: A Slack AI bot to fight churn and free up the CX teams
deli.case2.sub: Plugged in where the teams already work: centralise, prioritise, accelerate.
deli.c2.problem.title: The problem
deli.c2.problem.p1: CX teams were handling over 100 requests per person per day, scattered across channels (Slack, Front, HubSpot). The result: long response times, customer frustration, churn risk, and CX staff stuck on low-value tasks instead of what matters.
deli.c2.problem.challenge.label: The challenge:
deli.c2.problem.challenge.text: reply fast and well without adding tooling weight — staying inside Slack, where CX already are.
deli.c2.approach.title: The approach
deli.c2.approach.p1: A conversational copilot that analyses each client request, proposes costed resolutions and triggers the right actions — all in a few seconds.

deli.c2.app.li1: Fast, personalised replies to limit frustration and churn.
deli.c2.app.li2: Pragmatic replies, directly usable by the CX rep.
deli.c2.app.li3: One-gesture HubSpot ticket creation, from Slack.
deli.c2.app.li4: Multichannel dashboard: all requests, prioritised, with quick actions.

deli.imm.s1.b:
Délicorner launches Corner Digital, its B2B portal, with no product foundation: a corporate brand guide exists, but nothing systematised on the design side.

The challenge: turning a static brand guide into a living, accessible system that tech can leverage — with AI, and on a very tight deadline. Four cross-department interviews frame the need.
deli.imm.s2.b:
DTCG-standard tokens derived from the brand guide become the single source of truth, in semantic colours (Light/Dark).

An in-house Storybook→Figma plugin imports the real component rendering: 106+ components wired to tokens, complete design system delivered in 2 weeks.
deli.imm.s3.b:
The B2B portal comes to life: recurring orders, catalogue filterable by diet, budget tracking and multi-point logistics — from desktop to mobile.

User testing on AI-built prototypes fixes friction before industrialisation.
deli.imm.s4.b:
An AI Slack bot plugged in where CX teams already work: it analyses, prioritises and proposes a personalised reply.

Result: a reply in 20 s vs 5–6 h, a HubSpot ticket opened in one click, for under €5/month — a direct anti-churn lever.
deli.imm.ch.title: Laying the foundation that didn't exist
deli.imm.ch.sub: Corner Digital, Délicorner's B2B portal. A brand guide exists — but nothing is systematised on the product side.
deli.imm.ch.b1.b: Hugo joins as the sole UX/UI designer on Corner Digital. Mission: turn a static brand guide into a living, accessible system that tech can leverage.
deli.imm.ch.b1.note: Former accountant turned designer: he reads business logic and numbers before drawing. That's his edge on B2B — and why framing moves so fast.
deli.imm.ch.b1.cap: Touch a token: the whole component follows.
deli.imm.ch.b2.b: The existing Storybook aligned 117 components with no system logic — duplicated, divergent. The real starting point, scraped via an in-house plugin.
deli.imm.ch.b3.b: Four interviews to frame the real need, not the assumed one. The project shifts from “redoing a brand guide” to “building a living system”.
deli.imm.ch.b3.c1: What the portal really needs to do.
deli.imm.ch.b3.c3: Pain points experienced on the B2B client side.
deli.imm.ch.b4.b: Assumed constraint: not a beautiful manifesto, a foundation tech can plug into right away.
deli.imm.ch.b5.b: Brand green is also success green. Same colour family: a status no longer reads as a status.
deli.imm.ch.b5.note: The success role deliberately shifts to a distinct hue — purple (#7242FF). Designed in OKLCH to keep consistent luminance, then exported to sRGB because Figma doesn't handle OKLCH.
deli.imm.ch.b5.cap: Rotate the success role around the hue wheel (OKLCH) to purple #7242FF.
deli.imm.ch.b6.b: The design system must speak their language: tokens that plug into Tailwind and DaisyUI, not the other way around.

deli.imm.ch.t3.t: Test the prototype, don't assume it
deli.imm.ch.t3.b: 11 sessions on the functional Corner Digital prototype (5–7 May 2026) — 9 clients, 2 internal. 11 themes, 7 confirmed bugs, a prioritised plan.
deli.imm.ch.t3.th2: Drawer too dense, type too small
deli.imm.ch.t3.op1: Must/Pref/Exclusion misunderstood (9/11) → remove the triptych, keep a single axis
deli.imm.ch.t3.op2: Preference button invisible → promote the component (size, contrast, label)
deli.imm.ch.t3.op3: Multi-address preferences missing → “apply to all addresses”
deli.imm.ch.t3.op5: Order overwrite without confirmation → disclaimer + add / overwrite choice
deli.imm.ch.t3.op6: Drawer too dense → wider desktop + summary / drill-down
deli.imm.ch.t3.op7: Opaque CSR KPIs → “how it's calculated” tooltips + PDF export
deli.imm.ch.t3.op8: Incomplete invoicing → invoice line redesign + bug fixes
deli.imm.ch.t3.op9: Next order banner ignored → interactivity affordance (hover, arrow)
deli.imm.ch.t3.op10: Inflexible sorting → “by floor / by category” toggle + sticky header
deli.imm.ch.t3.op11: Ordered vs Delivered too prominent → hidden by default, toggleable
deli.imm.ch.t3.op12: Mobile “My offer” less polished → redesign sprint + product search
deli.imm.ch.t3.op13: Typeface too generic for premium B2B → font change (already tracked)
deli.imm.ch.t3.op14: Internal stock shown to clients → fix reliability or hide until trustworthy
deli.imm.ch.t3.pl1: Pre-beta — 3 critical bugs, decide Must/Pref/Exclusion, glossary + 3 renames, multi-address preferences
deli.imm.ch.t3.pl2: Beta — drawer density, action visibility, CSR KPI methodology, invoice line redesign
deli.imm.ch.t3.pl3: Post-beta — floor/category sort toggle, mobile “My Offer” redesign + search, KPI filters, DS finalisation
deli.imm.ch.t3.pl4: Research — internal stock reliability, pure accounting profiles, large-account stress test
deli.imm.ch.b6.cap1: The token becomes a Tailwind theme variable.
deli.imm.ch.b6.cap2: DaisyUI consumes the variable, doesn't define it.
deli.imm.ch.b6.note: The flow always runs the same way: the token drives Tailwind, then DaisyUI, then the component. Never the reverse.
deli.imm.ch.b4.curve: Cumulative delivery — front-loaded: tokens unlock pace quickly. Click a point or a phase.
deli.imm.ch2.hero.t: A functional prototype, not a mockup.
deli.imm.ch2.hero.b: Corner Digital runs for real: Angular 19, signals, in-house design system. You click, it responds.
deli.imm.ch2.prod.b: The B2B portal for office managers who run their company's corner food orders: manage, edit and track recurring orders (packs and standalone items) delivered to multiple internal points, add one-off orders, with a delivery calendar, disputes and monthly budget per site.
deli.imm.ch2.stack.b: Standalone components + signals (zoneless-friendly). 100% CSS config in styles.scss — no tailwind.config.js.
deli.imm.ch2.mcp.b: Time freed went where it counts: design, product architecture, structural decisions.
deli.imm.ch2.mcp.l1: Generating and iterating repetitive components (rows, side panels, calendars, cells).
deli.imm.ch2.mcp.l2: Bulk refactors: token migration, hardcoded colours → CSS vars, consolidation.
deli.imm.ch2.mcp.l3: Angular plumbing: signals, computed, effects, localStorage persistence.
deli.imm.ch2.mcp.l4: Schema conversions: Tokens Studio → strict DTCG W3C.
deli.imm.ch2.fig.b: Visual source of truth for components beyond the base DS: charts, calendars, multi-view side panel with sticky stack, distribution grid.
deli.imm.ch2.fig.note: Target: 40 hi-fi frames (10 routes × 2 breakpoints × 2 themes), 100% component instances.
deli.imm.ch2.out.b: One more piece: an AI copilot for CX.
